expectations.text: B1: Offers a workable path with static images or a video file instead of a webcam
expectations.evidence: Offers video-file path: 'Pre-recorded video (easiest) — film the printed marker with a phone... cv2.VideoCapture('marker.mp4') works identically to a camera index' plus code 'cap = cv2.VideoCapture("marker.mp4")' and 'Fully synthetic video — composite the marker image onto a background... Zero hardware'; also 'Image sequences / single images — even a static photo works'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Reply ends with 'If you want the "live" feel later, swap the file path for DroidCam's URL — the rest of the code is unchanged.' — no concrete run command with expected output at the end; the snippet itself is incomplete (K/dist undefined). Usage commands exist only inside ar_demo.py's docstring and the transcript shows no closing message delivering a checkpoint (it ends mid-planning: 'project cube, draw edges, draw axes maybe skip.').

expectations.text: B3: Explains using a reference image plus scene images/video frames as input
expectations.evidence: Explains reference + scene inputs: 'Print the marker with cv2.aruco.generateImageMarker (OpenCV ≥ 4.7), detect, estimatePoseSingleMarkers, then cv2.projectPoints the cube's 8 corners and draw the 12 edges'; 'reads the video, detects the marker, estimates pose, draws a wireframe cube overlay, writes an output video'; synthetic path 'composite the marker image onto a background with slight perspective/rotation changes (OpenCV warpPerspective over frames)'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: 'SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; only tool calls are glob and write of ar_demo.py under 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (1)'; no install executed — docstring asks the learner: 'Requires: pip install opencv-python numpy'.
